issues.description: ACL root invariant change is not stated; reader must reconstruct semantics from code
issues.detail: The semantics of `a.root` changed from a boolean ("is root policy, root namespace only") to a `*namespace.Namespace` ("is root policy, attached to this ancestor namespace"). The new invariant — that a request is root-allowed iff the request's namespace `HasParent(a.root)` — is the load-bearing security property of this PR. The comment on the struct field mentions "non-nil namespace if the 'root' named policy ... is present" but does not state the ancestor/parent rule, nor what `HasParent` returns for the same namespace (reflexive? strict?). A literate-programming-grade invariant comment is required here because the ACL fast-path is exactly the kind of code a serious reader will study and the kind of code where an off-by-one in ancestry semantics is a privilege-escalation bug.

issues.description: HasParent semantics not audited at the call site; reflexivity is the security hinge
issues.detail: `if !ns.HasParent(a.root) { return ret }` — this single line decides whether a token bearing a root policy issued in namespace N can act in namespace M. The correctness of the change depends entirely on whether `HasParent` is reflexive (N is a parent of N) so that a root token in N still works in N, and whether it is strict-ancestor or includes-self in the way the test expects. Neither this PR's diff nor its comment audits that. The test only covers (root ns, root ns) and (child ns, child ns) plus the negative (child-root acting from root) — it does not test (grandchild acting under child-root), nor (sibling), nor (same-ns), which are the cases where the ancestor predicate's exact semantics matter. Either state the invariant in code or add the table-driven test.

issues.description: NamespaceSealed is a stub that always returns false and is wired into ListAllNamespaces and an exported method
issues.detail: `(*Core).NamespaceSealed` returns `false` unconditionally with a TODO. That is fine as scaffolding, but the description claims `ListAllNamespaces` is "adjusted ... including sealed namespaces in the response (currently stubbed with NamespaceSealed stub)." The reader cannot tell from the diff what the contract of this method is supposed to be — is it "is this exact namespace sealed," or "is any ancestor in the direct line sealed"? The doc comment says "in direct ancestry line" which is a different predicate than the name suggests. Until SealManager lands, the stub silently makes "sealed" indistinguishable from "unsealed" everywhere it is consulted; any caller that branches on it today is dead code. State the intended contract in the comment so the eventual SealManager implementer is forced to match it, and consider returning an error or panicking in tests if the stub is reached in a path that would change behavior post-implementation.

issues.description: response_util.go refactor reuses an unrelated hce variable in a switch that no longer needs it pre-declared
issues.detail: The refactor from a series of `if` blocks to a `switch` is a readability win, but `var hce HTTPCodedError = &codedError{}` is now declared above the switch purely so the `case errwrap.ContainsType(err, hce)` clause can reference it. The lifetime and purpose of `hce` are not obvious from the new layout — it looks like a sentinel for type matching but is constructed as a concrete `&codedError{}`. A reader who has not seen the old code will not understand why an empty `codedError` is being instantiated. Either inline the type via `errwrap.ContainsType(err, (*codedError)(nil))` style, or add a one-line comment that says "sentinel value used only for type identity in errwrap.ContainsType/GetType."

issues.description: ErrNamespaceSealed string-contains check will false-match on user-controlled error text
issues.detail: `errwrap.Contains(err, consts.ErrNamespaceSealed.Error())` matches on the substring "namespace is sealed." That string is short, generic, and exactly the kind of message a backend or a policy error might legitimately include in a wrapped error chain without meaning the sentinel. Combined with `ErrSealed` ("Vault is sealed") in the same `case`, both errors now map to 503. The asymptotically-fine substring match has a constant-factor footgun: any error whose message happens to contain "namespace is sealed" will be downgraded to 503 even if it should be 400 or 500. Prefer `errors.Is(err, consts.ErrNamespaceSealed)` if the sentinel is wrapped with `%w`, and reserve substring matching for the legacy cases that already depend on it.

issues.description: NSTokenLength described as `(TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID)` in the PR description but not visible in the diff
issues.detail: The PR description introduces `NSTokenLength` as `(TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID)`. That expression is not a length formula — `"."[1]` is out of bounds for a 1-byte string in Go and would not compile; the author likely meant `len(".")` (which is 1) or `TokenLen + 1 + len(nsID)`. Either the description is wrong or the actual constant in code disagrees with the description. A reader auditing the token format would be misled. Reconcile the description with the code and state the token layout (TokenLen bytes, one '.' separator, nsID) in a comment where the constant is defined.

issues.description: leaseView / tokenIndexView lose the root-namespace special case without a comment justifying equivalence
issues.detail: Previously these methods branched: root namespace used `systemBarrierView.SubView(...)`, non-root used `namespaceMountEntryView(...)`. The new code uses `NamespaceView(m.core.barrier, ns).SubView(...)` for all namespaces including root. The reader has to trust that `NamespaceView(barrier, RootNamespace).SubView(systemBarrierPrefix+...)` produces the same storage path as `systemBarrierView.SubView(...)` did. If it does, this is a clean simplification and worth a one-line comment stating the equivalence. If it does not, existing root-namespace leases become unreachable. Either way, the audit needs to be on the record.

issues.description: ListAllNamespaces callers switched to ListNamespaces without stating the semantic difference
issues.detail: Four call sites in `core.go`, `core_metrics.go`, and `counters.go` changed from `c.namespaceStore.ListAllNamespaces(ctx, true)` to `c.ListNamespaces(ctx)`. The boolean `true` had a meaning (presumably "include sealed" or "recursive") that is now hidden inside `ListNamespaces`. Readers auditing MFA enforcement, locked-user updates, entity gauge collection, and active token counting need to know whether sealed namespaces are now included or excluded in each call site, because the answer changes which namespaces contribute to metrics and which get their locked-user state refreshed. Add a one-line comment at the `ListNamespaces` definition stating its contract relative to sealed namespaces.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The PR's load-bearing change is the ACL root fast-path: `a.root` flipped from `bool` to `*namespace.Namespace`, and authorization now hinges on `ns.HasParent(a.root)`. The new invariant — root token issued in ancestor N grants root in descendant M — is not stated in code, and the test only covers same-namespace cases plus one negative; the ancestor/reflexivity semantics that decide the security property are not exercised. NamespaceSealed is a `return false` stub wired into multiple consult sites with an unclear contract (\"direct ancestry line\" per its comment, but the name suggests \"this namespace\"), and ListAllNamespaces callers were silently switched to ListNamespaces with no audit of whether sealed namespaces are now included. The response_util refactor is a readability win but adds a `consts.ErrNamespaceSealed` substring match on a short generic string that will false-match on any error containing \"namespace is sealed\" — prefer `errors.Is`. Algorithmic complexity is unchanged; the issues are invariant, contract, and literate-comment debt at exactly the places where the next maintainer will need them.
